name: Libya
headline: Libya: +15.9% growth in 2025, 1.8% inflation, debt 154% of GDP
sections: Libya is a $44.7 billion economy (2025), the world's 104th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +15.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $17K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K.

Consumer prices rose 1.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.5% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 18.8% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 50.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 154% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 238% in 2020. The general government balance is −30.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +1.1% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 138% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 174% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 71.1 years (2024). Population: 7.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
